To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the ion focusing and the ion transport effect of the buffer gas in the RF electric field driven ion funnel is properly accounted for by using the SIMION program incorporating the Douglas ion-neutral drag coefficient model; 2) the low-m/z ion cutoff behavior is approximated by an effective potential model; and 3) a modified ion funnel configuration, with a DC field and an RF field applied to different regions, is proposed to increase the ion transmission efficiency.
the m/z transmission properties of the ion funnel is determined by the ion-neutral collision frequency, the ion focusing effect, and the RF and DC fields.
we have characterized the transmission properties of the ion funnel using SIMION and the results compare favorably to the experimental results of Smith et al.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new ion funnel configuration, which has been shown to improve the transmission efficiency for low m/z ions.
the ion funnel transmission properties and their applications to the ion mobility spectrometry (IMS) and the ion trap mass analyzer (ITMA).
the development of a new ion funnel for mass spectrometry applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ion funnel has a transmission window with a sharp cutoff at the high mass end, a broad transmission window at the low mass end, and an intermediate transmission window at the center.
the ion focusing effect of the background buffer gas is the dominant mechanism in the low-m/z ion transmission window.
a radio frequency ion funnel can provide a very efficient and effective means for ion focusing and transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ion transmission properties are determined by the combined effect of the driving fields, ion-neutral collisional focusing, and the ion-neutral collisional energy loss.
the ion funnel is a versatile ion transmission device, which can be easily tuned to meet a variety of ion transmission requirements.
a proper understanding of the transmission properties of the ion funnel is essential for the successful design of an electrospray mass spectrometer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ion-neutral drag coefficient model can be incorporated into the SIMION ion optics software package for ion focusing and transport simulation.

the ion transmission characteristics can be predicted by the SIMION ion optics simulation program, and the ion focusing and transporting effect of the background neutral gas can be properly accounted for by incorporating the appropriate ion-neutral collisional model.
the ion funnel can be used to transmit ions with a broad m/z range.
